So then, another time, he saw me looking at a trumpet, backstage in the Regal Theater in Chicago. So it was an Olds, so I was looking at this Olds, and the guy brought down about three of them from the shop, and I was looking at them and he passed by and saw it, and he says, "You going to buy a horn?" I says, "I'm thinking about it." If I could pick out the one which I liked the best. So he says, "Now, if you're going to buy that, tell Mr. Wright." He was the manager, the road manager. He said, "Tell Mr. Wright…

borrow 200 for six months," and he said, "I can't get it." He said, "I can't get it. I've been trying." I said, "That ain't nothing over here." I said, "The guys don't do it over here because they don't want to get stuck. They're scared that they might be stuck and they'll want to leave, but they'll be in debt, then, you know." I said, "The cats won't do it, but they can get it."
